name: Conditional Inversion / Membership-Propagation Law Candidate
claim_form: When a recurring implementation family is represented as an explicit closed set across multiple semantic surfaces, concentrating family membership and dispatch behind a stable typed boundary can trade a one-time coordination/setup cost for lower marginal propagation burden on later family additions. The sign is conditional, not universal.

candidate_variables.M: expected number/rate of future same-family additions or changes
candidate_variables.S: shared mechanism fraction across family members
candidate_variables.B: strength of an already-existing stable polymorphic boundary
candidate_variables.R: later propagation reduction attributable to concentration of membership knowledge

qualitative_prediction: Higher F can increase the opportunity for propagation reduction.
Higher S can increase the opportunity for shared abstraction without erasing semantics.
Higher H can reduce or reverse abstraction benefit by forcing leaky special cases.
Strong pre-existing B can make a second inversion layer redundant or harmful.
Low expected future M can leave K unrepaid even if later marginal changes are cheaper.
falsifiers_or_boundary_evidence: DIRECT remains no worse under later same-family additions despite high F and high S.
INVERT requires provider-specific escape hatches whose burden grows with H.
The abstraction reduces textual duplication but not semantic propagation surfaces.
The boundary causes invalid behavior, hidden coupling, or broader unrelated edits.
Outcome sign changes primarily with deployment/UI/schema boundaries rather than dependency direction itself.
relation_to_SOLID: DIP/OCP are treated as named design interventions or mechanism families, not axioms. Evidence may support a bounded support domain, a reversal domain, or abstention rather than the principle itself.
anti_replication_rule: Additional projects are scientifically useful only when they alter or discriminate a predeclared moderator, mechanism, or boundary. Same-sign repetition without moderator gain is not cumulative authority by itself.
authority: No outcome has been observed. CIL-C1 is a falsifiable organizing hypothesis for P10 and future cross-project worlds.
